profiles.label: Microsoft Excel
profiles.description: A workbook with a Data sheet (numbers stored as numbers, real dates, one header row, frozen header, filters), a Report sheet describing the sources, rules and steps, and a Log sheet with the audit log.

profiles.label: Databases, Python, R, BI tools (CSV)
profiles.description: UTF-8 CSV without a byte-order mark: comma-separated, ISO dates, "." as decimal separator, header "Name [unit]".

profiles.label: Python, Spark, DuckDB, data lakes (Parquet)
profiles.description: Apache Parquet with one typed column per field: numbers as doubles, whole numbers as 64-bit integers, dates as dates, date-times as UTC timestamps; column names "Name [unit]".

profiles.label: QGIS / ArcGIS / web maps (GeoJSON)
profiles.description: An RFC 7946 GeoJSON FeatureCollection in WGS84 longitude/latitude, built from the geometry column or the latitude and longitude columns.

profiles.label: QGIS / ArcGIS (Shapefile)
profiles.description: An ESRI Shapefile (.shp, .shx, .dbf) in the coordinate reference system of the data, with its .prj (ESRI WKT) and .cpg (UTF-8), and data.fields.csv, which maps each field name of 10 characters to the full column name and unit.

profiles.label: Google Earth (KML)
profiles.description: A KML 2.2 file in WGS 84 longitude and latitude: one placemark per row, named by its ID column, with every column as extended data and the geometry, or the point of the latitude and longitude columns.

profiles.label: QGIS / ArcGIS / GDAL (FlatGeobuf)
profiles.description: A FlatGeobuf file in the coordinate reference system of the data, recorded by its EPSG code: one feature per row, in row order, with any mix of geometry kinds and every column as a typed property named "Name [unit]". No field-name or 2 GB limits, so it is also what a Shapefile too large for its format is delivered as.
